title: The New Rules of Economic Warfare
gist: This is an FP Live event promo page rather than a full article: it previews an August 4, 2026 interview with former State Department sanctions official Edward Fishman on his 'Chokepoints' thesis that the United States built an economic-warfare playbook now being turned against it. The only other substantive content is a promo blurb for a Daniel Yergin session describing the Strait of Hormuz shut down, Houthi attempts to block Saudi Red Sea exports, unrestored global crude inventories and possible Chinese export-curb relaxation.

themes.theme: Chokepoints as the new economic weapon

insights.claim: U.S.-China export controls and the Houthis' ability to disrupt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb are two expressions of the same phenomenon: the embrace of chokepoints as an economic weapon.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Treat semiconductor export controls and maritime interdiction as one asset class of risk — both price the same scarcity of physical and technological transit points.
insights.quote: Both represent the embrace of chokepoints as an economic weapon.

insights.claim: Edward Fishman argues in Chokepoints: American Power in the Age of Economic Warfare that the United States built an economic-warfare playbook that is now being used against it, whether offensively or in self-defense.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Boomerang risk on US-designed sanctions architecture argues for pricing in retaliatory export controls on critical minerals, software and payment rails.
insights.quote: he argues that the United States built a playbook that is now being used against it, whether offensively or in self-defense
insights.locator: Edward Fishman deployed these very tools

insights.claim: The claim carries unusual practitioner weight because Fishman personally deployed these tools while serving in the U.S. Defense, State and Treasury Departments and was a top sanctions official at the State Department during the Obama administration.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Insider-authored critiques of sanctions efficacy are the leading indicator of policy rethink inside Treasury and State.

themes.theme: Energy shock backdrop flagged in the companion session

insights.claim: Oil prices are rising again with the Strait of Hormuz once again shut down and the Houthis attempting to block Saudi exports through the Red Sea, and this time prices may not come down quickly.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Simultaneous closure of Hormuz and Red Sea export routes removes the usual mean-reversion assumption from crude — favors structurally long energy positioning.
insights.quote: Oil prices are once again on the rise—and this time, they may not come down so quickly.

insights.claim: Global reservoirs of crude have not been restored, amplifying the price impact of the current supply-route disruptions, while China may drop its export curbs.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Low starting inventories mean any incremental supply outage translates near one-for-one into price — asymmetric upside risk in crude.
